inscriptions.inscription:
The 10 scenes on the four prints are identified by their titles: 
Print one: 1. Remnant Snow on Broken Bridge (Duanqiao canxue, 斷橋殘雪), 2. Lotus Breeze at Qu Winery (Quyuan fenghe, 曲院風河 [sic]). 
Print two: 3. Autumn Moon over Placid Lake (Pinghu qiuyue, 平湖秋月), 4. Twin Peaks Piercing the Clouds (Liangfeng chayun, 兩峰插云), 5. Spring Dawn at Su Dike (Sudi chunxiao, 蘇 堤春曉), 11. The emperor’s temporary palace (xinggong, 行宮). 
Print three: 6. Listening to the Orioles by the Willow Ripples (Liulang wenying, 柳浪 聞鶯), 7. Three Stupas and the Reflecting Moon (Santan yinyue, 三潭印月). 
Print four: 8. Watching Fish at Flower Cove (Huagang guanyu, 花港觀魚), 9. Sunset at Leifeng Pagoda (Leifeng xizhao, 雷峰夕照). 10. Evening Bell from Nanping Hill (Nanping wanzhong, 南屏晚鍾.) 
In print two, 11. the emperor’s temporary palace (xinggong 行宮) is also identified.

description:
Mount Putuo, an island southeast of Shanghai that covers approximately 12.5 square kilometers (4.8 square miles), is one of the Four Sacred Buddhist Mountains and a destination for the worship of Guanyin (Avalokiteśhvara), the bodhisattva of compassion.

The importance of Putuo as a national and international pilgrimage center began in the 900s and was revived in the late 1500s and 1600s. Its attraction is partly based on the claim that Putuo Island is Mount Potalaka, the home of Guanyin located on the southern coast of India, which made the island attractive to Korean and Japanese pilgrims as well. Mount Putuo received imperial visits and patronage from the Kangxi and Qianlong emperors.

inscriptions.inscription:
The 10 scenes on the four prints are identified by their titles: 
Print one: 1. Remnant Snow on Broken Bridge (Duanqiao canxue, 斷橋殘雪), 2. Lotus Breeze at Qu Winery (Quyuan fenghe, 曲院風河 [sic]). 
Print two: 3. Autumn Moon over Placid Lake (Pinghu qiuyue, 平湖秋月), 4. Twin Peaks Piercing the Clouds (Liangfeng chayun, 兩峰插云), 5. Spring Dawn at Su Dike (Sudi chunxiao, 蘇 堤春曉), 11. The emperor’s temporary palace (xinggong, 行宮). 
Print three: 6. Listening to the Orioles by the Willow Ripples (Liulang wenying, 柳浪 聞鶯), 7. Three Stupas and the Reflecting Moon (Santan yinyue, 三潭印月). 
Print four: 8. Watching Fish at Flower Cove (Huagang guanyu, 花港觀魚), 9. Sunset at Leifeng Pagoda (Leifeng xizhao, 雷峰夕照). 10. Evening Bell from Nanping Hill (Nanping wanzhong, 南屏晚鍾.) 
In print two, 11. the emperor’s temporary palace (xinggong 行宮) is also identified.

description: Revived by the southern imperial inspection tours, West Lake imagery became a popular subject during the early Qing dynasty. This panorama is composed of four prints, showing the Ten Scenes of the West Lake in Hangzhou along with other sights. The vanishing point perspective and the hatching lines that depict shading, water, or sky derive from European copperplate prints, introduced by missionaries to China, and were celebrated novelties in 18th-century Suzhou prints.
